findings.claim: The guarded watch stream does not terminate immediately after an authorization revocation error; it can remain pending until another store event arrives.
findings.evidence: Acceptance B requires the watch stream to return PERMISSION_DENIED and terminate after revocation, but the new code wraps the stream with `checked.scan(true, ...)`: on the first `Err` it sets `*active = false` and returns `Some(item)`, while `None` is only returned by the scan closure when the upstream stream yields a later item. A live broadcast stream with no later events will leave subsequent polls pending rather than terminated.
findings.suggested_fix: Replace the `scan` wrapper with a stream adapter that emits the first error and then returns `None` on the next poll without waiting for another upstream item, or make the per-event authorization failure close the underlying watch channel explicitly.
